records.c: Fifteen zero bytes at the beginning of the resident load, ahead of the stage selection workspace at $0810.
Base address for the per-player stage indices at offsets one and two, read by stage setup at $1A75.
Player one's zero-based stage index. Cleared at $19FD and advanced through the indexed increment at $1C7A.
Player two's zero-based stage index. Cleared at $1A00 and read at $1A75 with X=2.
Selected stage index copied from the active player's entry at $1A78. Indexes the stage header fields during setup.
Base address for the per-player mission numbers at offsets one and two. Stage setup compares the selected entry with $FCC0.
Player one's mission number. Initialized from $FCC0 and compared with the loaded mission at $1A41.
Player two's mission number. Initialized from $FCC0 and compared with the loaded mission at $1A49.
Per-player stage-progress state table. The finish routine shifts the active entry at $1BE0.
First bonus carry-in byte. The bonus setup at $AF6B copies it to $AEE9.
Second bonus carry-in byte. The bonus setup at $AF71 copies it to $AEEA.
Participant countdown initialized from $257B minus one. The mission-switch check compares it with one. The life-loss path decrements it and returns to the attract loop when it reaches zero.
At $1A57 the switch path saves the loaded mission number plus one here before calling the bonus initializer. The consumer of the saved value remains open.
Four frame values selected with the low two bits of the animation counter at $0822.
Shared animation bit toggled with XOR $02 at $3CF8.
Frame offset selected from the four-byte table at $081C.
Running animation counter whose low two bits select the entry at $081C.
Animation step that wraps at four in the shared divider routine. The panel code reads it at $26C3.
Animation step that wraps at six in the shared divider routine. The player code reads it at $2F5A.
Shared animation divider. Counts down at $3CEE and reloads with five at expiry.
Previous mixed byte used as an input to the next raster-based random-number calculation at $0839.
Incrementing byte mixed into the raster-based random-number calculation. Incremented between the reads of $D012 and $D011.
Modulus supplied in A at $0829. The subtraction loop reduces the mixed byte below this value.

Mixes the input in A with the incrementing counter at $0827, the VIC raster registers and the prior accumulator at $0826. Stores the mixed byte at $0826 and subtracts the original input repeatedly until the remainder is smaller or zero. Callers pass a nonzero divisor.
Five loaded zero bytes before the active stage width at $0850.
Width of the selected stage in metatiles. The row pointer builder adds it to each source pointer as the row stride.
Height of the selected stage in metatiles. The setup at $0B9F uses it to calculate the vertical scroll limit.
High byte of the horizontal origin limit, built by rotating the carries from the two left shifts at $0B89 and $0B8D.
Low byte of the horizontal origin limit. Setup computes the low byte of four times the stage width minus 38.
High byte of the vertical origin limit, built by rotating the carries from the two shifts at $0BA6 and $0BAA.
Low byte of the vertical origin limit, four times the stage height minus 24.
Thirty-two low address bytes generated for the active stage tile rows. The row stride is the width at $0850.
High address bytes paired with the tile row table at $0856.
Thirty-two low address bytes generated for the active stage attribute rows. The movement and map scanners index them by metatile row.
High address bytes paired with the attribute row table at $0896.

Split dictionary pointers for 240 metatile IDs. At $17C3 and $17C8 the initial screen renderer reads low bytes at $08D6 and high bytes at $09C6. Entry n addresses $C000 plus 16 times n, where the four rows of four character indices start.
High bytes of the 240 dictionary addresses paired with $08D6. The table advances one page for each group of sixteen tile IDs.
High bytes of 22 colour RAM row addresses, used with $947C for panel and scene drawing.
First two entries of the projectile facing table. The launcher stores the player's facing byte here and the update uses it to choose horizontal movement.
Direction code for the extra attack slot, set to one or two by the two facing branches at $B8AA and $B8C3.
Projectile plane copied from $39E3 at launch. The draw routine tests it when setting projectile sprite priority.
Second projectile plane. The sprite-priority setup at $2357 reads this slot and leaves priority bit three clear when the plane equals one.
Horizontal movement step saved from X by the projectile updater at $2282 and added or subtracted from the shot position.
Projectile mode byte. A nonzero value raises the base horizontal step from four to five at $227B.
Per-projectile state checked before overlay collision tests and set when a hit or obstacle has consumed a shot.
Per-shot flag. A nonzero entry bypasses the projectile terrain test at $22AB.
Second projectile flag in the pair based at $0AD8. The sprite preparation and recovery paths can clear it with the first.
Current active-low input mask. The joystick read at $3B84, keyboard merge and demo playback can write it.
Previous merged input byte saved at $3BF6. The attract handler at $98CA reads it to detect directional input.
Incoming accumulator saved by the stage setup entry at $0AF1.
Active stage parameter from the indexed header at $FCF1, copied to this byte and $0BE0.
Projectile launch delay for slot zero. The launcher stores four and the update at $228C counts it down.
Launch delay for projectile slot one, the second entry of the array beginning at $0AEB.

Uses the stage index at $0813 to select colours, display setup values and both grid bases. Builds 32 row pointers for each grid. Derives the viewport limits and the bottom coordinate used by later rendering from the cached width and height.

Fills four split tables at $0856, $0876, $0896 and $08B6 with the tile and attribute addresses of 32 rows, adding the stage width each time. Then computes horizontal and vertical bounds in character-cell units.
High bytes of the actors' horizontal positions. The screen and contact routines combine them with the low bytes at $0BE3.
Secondary horizontal high bytes initialized from the spawn cursor at $89BD. The raster shadow copy at $1D04 pairs them with $0BE7.
High bytes of the horizontal spawn anchors, initialized with the live X by $89C0. Actor updates compare these with current positions.
High byte of the player's X coordinate. The projectile launcher and character-coordinate conversion both read it with the player's X low byte.
High bytes of the first two projectile X positions. The launcher propagates the carry or borrow from the low-byte offset into this indexed field.
High byte of the auxiliary attack X coordinate. The fire handler writes it after adding or subtracting 24 from the player X position.
Fourth slot of the high X table starting at $0BCA. The launch and movement routines index it by projectile slot.
Two initial zero bytes between the four projectile X high fields and the first actor Y at $0BD0.
Y coordinate of actor slot zero. The active-slot scan at $9D24 skips zero coordinates.
Remaining three actor Y positions after slot zero at $0BD0. The slot clearer at $18B6 writes zero to all four entries.
Player sprite cropping baseline. In Mission 2 stage index two, the sprite preparation subtracts player Y from this value and handles a difference below sixteen.
Six initial zero bytes between the single player crop-baseline field and the player Y coordinate at $0BDB.
Player Y in pixels. The coordinate conversion at $390C subtracts the top margin and divides by eight.
Live Y coordinate of projectile slot zero. The mid-flight updater treats zero as a vacant slot.
Live Y coordinate of projectile slot one, indexed from $0BDC.
Extra attack slot Y. The hit check stores the player Y minus six at $B88D.
Vertical split position derived from the stage parameter. The actor clamping path at $2704 reads it and adds 12 to get the lower group threshold.
Low bytes of the horizontal positions. Movement changes these bytes and propagates carry or borrow to $0BBD.
Secondary horizontal low bytes initialized at spawn and copied into the raster shadow at $1CB3.
Low bytes of actor spawn anchors. Multiple movement handlers check how far the actor has moved from this position.
Low byte of the player horizontal position. The terrain probe and horizontal position updater read it.
Low horizontal coordinate for each projectile. The movement loop adds or subtracts the selected horizontal step.

Per-actor low X anchors. The vertical update compares an airborne actor's current low X to its anchor to decide when to toggle the direction bits. The contact code also uses the first byte for the auxiliary attack X.
Player X in half-resolution units. The actor collision routines compare their X coordinates against it.
Low bytes of the vertical positions, incremented before carrying into the pixel Y at $0BD0.
Fractional horizontal position bytes. The walker at $A0BC adds $60 and moves the whole position when the fraction carries.
Screen row index by projectile slot. The Mission 2 backdrop test reads this table before fetching a row address.
Screen column index by projectile slot. Mission 2 adds this column to its chosen screen row.
First actor type byte. The updater at $9D63 uses the selected type to index the split handler table.
Type bytes for actor slots one through three. The updater reads them through $0C07,X.
Secondary sprite colours by actor slot. The raster handler loads them into VIC sprite five's colour register.
Two initial zero bytes following the four actor secondary sprite colour fields. The frame fields start at $0C11.
Per-actor sprite pointer or frame selector. Movement and animation handlers write it before drawing the actor.
Secondary frame pointer by actor slot, initialized to $55 and copied into the raster shadow at $1D46.
Another companion frame pointer by actor slot, initialized to $55 and copied into the raster shadow at $1D4A.
Signed integer part of the actor's vertical speed. The motion update adds it and the fractional carry to Y.
Low byte of the actor's vertical speed. The motion updater adds $80 and carries into the whole speed in $0C1D.
First terrain mask compared with actor orientation in the vertical movement path at $3D3F.
Per-actor facing or terrain mask. The update and contact routines compare it with directional masks.
Second terrain mask used in the corresponding test at $3D4A.
Actor movement flag set by the launch and vertical motion paths. Several overlays use it to select airborne frames or wait for landing.
Type-dependent state or countdown set from $9BEC when the actor is placed and overwritten by actor-specific actions.
Per-type auxiliary state copied from $9BFA by the placement initializer.
Per-type initial state copied from $9C08 for the slot.
Per-slot counter cleared by the initializers at $9C76 and $9C85.
Per-slot phase cleared or set to one by the placement jump table.
Per-slot timer decremented by $9D54 when active. That path calls $9D85 instead of selecting the ordinary type handler.
Player contact cooldown. The contact scanner at $BAF0 tests it and the input handler at $3BF9 suppresses input while it is active.
The update dispatcher tests for value one before restoring an actor's saved terrain marker for the applicable types.
Per-slot value initialized from $9C16.
Vertical boundary in character rows, calculated at $0BB9 as four times the stage height minus three.
Viewport horizontal origin low byte. Initial drawing copies it from $177F and a screen-page transition copies it from $0C5F.
Viewport horizontal origin high byte. Initial drawing copies it from $1780 and a screen-page transition copies it from $0C60.
Low byte of the viewport's vertical origin in character rows.
High byte of the viewport's vertical origin. $392E adds the carry from the low-byte calculation to it.
Tile lookup horizontal cursor low byte. The resolver at $0C63 shifts the horizontal pair right by two to get the metatile column.
Tile lookup horizontal cursor high byte, rotated into the low byte by the metatile resolver.
Low byte of the tile lookup vertical cursor. The resolver shifts it right twice to select a metatile row.
High byte of the tile lookup vertical cursor. The initial draw propagates the carry here when it advances a screen row.
Pending low byte of the horizontal viewport origin, promoted to $0C57 on the screen-page change at $15EF.
Pending high byte of the horizontal viewport origin, promoted to $0C58 on the screen-page change.
Low byte of the pending vertical viewport origin, promoted to $0C59 when the screen page changes.
High byte of the pending vertical viewport origin. The bounds check at $12FE compares it against the high byte at $0854.
Divides the 16-bit horizontal and 8-bit vertical character coordinates by four. Adds the resulting column to the selected tile-row address and returns that 4 by 4 tile ID.

Scratch index shared by the scroll edge painters and the sprite motion sequencer at $2975. Edge redraw uses it for the coordinate within a 4-by-4 metatile. The sequencer uses it for the first motion record.
Counts the source metatiles crossed by the horizontal screen-edge writers.

Draws 40 characters at row 20 of the destination screen. Adds 20 to the viewport Y position, uses the metatile row pointers to find each pattern, and advances the source tile after crossing each four-column boundary.
Immediate metatile offset for the bottom edge character lookup at $0CE6.
High byte of the bottom edge's indexed screen store. The loop writes 40 cells, advancing to the next metatile at every fourth character column.
Draws 40 characters at row zero of the destination screen from the viewport origin. Resolves the source metatile's character row and advances the tile read when the within-tile column wraps.
Immediate metatile offset for the top edge character lookup at $0D5F.
High byte of the top edge's indexed screen store. The loop writes 40 cells, advancing to the next metatile at every fourth character column.

Draws 21 characters at column 39 of the destination screen. Uses the viewport X plus 39 to select a within-tile column and advances the grid pointer by its width after the bottom row of each source tile.

Patched metatile column operand for the ORA at $0DD9. The loop reads a character and moves the destination down by 40 cells. Advances one metatile row after the four character rows are used and returns after 21 screen rows.
Draws 21 characters at column zero of the destination screen. Uses the viewport origin to find the source tile and its character offset, advancing the screen pointer by 40 for each row.

Patched metatile column operand for the ORA at $0E68. The loop reads a character and moves the destination down by 40 cells. Advances one metatile row after the four character rows are used and returns after 21 screen rows.
Column remainder that bounds the horizontal colour edge pass. The loop compares it against the low two bits of the lookup cursor.

Positions the destination in colour RAM and the source in the stage tile grid. Uses the tile alignment byte at $0EA7 to locate the first tile edge. Expands tile IDs through the colour table at $CF00 and advances down the display.
Row remainder that bounds the vertical colour edge pass. The loop compares it with the low two bits of the vertical lookup cursor.
Starts from the view coordinates and writes to the colour RAM base at $D800. The row alignment operand at $1132 selects the starting edge within the four-character tile.

Reads metatile indices through $FB and colours through $CF00. Handles a partial first group from the viewport's within-tile column, then repeats each colour across four columns. Finishes the rightmost group at column 40.
Direction-indexed horizontal adjustment. Zero leaves X unchanged, one adds a character and the other nonzero value subtracts a character.
Direction-indexed vertical adjustment used by the Y calculation at $1262.
Copies the active viewport origin. Two direction-indexed tables choose whether each coordinate stays fixed or moves by one character in either direction, producing a proposed viewport in $0C5F–$0C62.
Replacement direction values indexed by the current direction and stored to both direction bytes when horizontal movement is clipped.
Replacement direction values used by the vertical boundary path, which restores the Y origin.

Cancels the requested scroll when $32 is nonzero. Otherwise compares the requested X and Y with the viewport limits and restores the active coordinate on a blocked axis. Tables $1291 and $1299 replace the requested directions with the remaining movement.
Low bytes of the eight screen-copy routines from $4800 to $4C00. The dispatcher writes the selected entry to $1484.
High bytes of the $4C00 screen-copy routines. The dispatcher installs the selected byte at $1485.
Low bytes of the eight screen-copy routines from $4C00 to $4800. The dispatcher writes the selected entry to $1496.
High bytes of the $4800 screen-copy routines. The dispatcher installs the selected byte at $1497.
Low bytes of the primary edge renderer targets, installed at $14C0 for the scroll direction in $14A4.
High bytes for the primary edge targets. $14BF calls the resulting address after $14DC reaches 6.
Low target bytes for the additional edge call at $14D3 when the matching high byte is nonzero.
High bytes for the additional edge call. A zero skips this call.
Selects the first colour update in $1390. The value 2 chooses the column routine at $0EA8. Other values choose $1133, and value 1 also requests the lower-row update at $8A53.
A nonzero byte requests a second call to $0EA8 after the first colour update.
Value for $1132, compared with the row coordinate modulo four before the row-based colour update proceeds.
Value for $0EA7, compared with the column coordinate modulo four as the colour-column routine adjusts its starting point.

Uses the direction in $13E0 to select colour RAM updates. Sets the tile alignment operands and chooses the row or column updater, with additional column and lower-row passes selected by the direction tables.
Direction index read by $1390 for colour RAM updates. The stage initializer sets this byte to $FF.
Direction for the page-to-page copy. $1465 replaces it with $FF after passing it to the edge renderer.
Flag tested at $1431 before calling the colour update at $1390. The caller clears this byte after the update.

Checks the stage outcome and the pending direction, scans the keyboard and returns to the attract loop when the selected key is pressed. Processes the gameplay update on raster flag one, services the deferred screen copy and edge redraws, then calls the actor and projectile update on flag two.
Return instruction between the attract-loop jump and the gameplay tick branch target at $1419.
Services the two phases signalled in $2B. Runs $157C on phase one, then performs pending screen work and runs $9384 on phase two. Skips back to the entry checks after the display page changes.
When a direction is pending and $14DC equals 4, chooses the destination screen from $2E and patches the matching copy call. Moves the direction index to $14A4 and clears the pending copy to $FF.
Low byte of the self-modified JSR at $1483.
High byte of the JSR target at $1483. It is written from the direction table before the call.
Low byte of the self-modified JSR at $1495.
High byte of the JSR target at $1495. The dispatcher writes $14A4 and clears $13E1 after either JSR returns.
Index passed from the screen-copy dispatcher to $14A5 for the subsequent edge redraw.

When $14DC is six, selects the edge redraw routines for the saved direction in $14A4. Patches the first call from $1350/$1358 and, if present, the second from $1360/$1368. Clears the pending direction after drawing.
Low address byte for the first patched call to an exposed-edge redraw routine.
High byte of the first patched scroll-edge call. After it returns, the dispatcher checks the second high-byte table and draws a second edge when its entry is nonzero.
Low address byte for the second patched call to an exposed-edge redraw routine.
High byte of the second patched scroll-edge call. Once the optional edge draw completes, sets the pending direction at $14A4 to $FF.
Scroll phase reduced modulo eight by $15E8. A zero phase promotes the next viewport origin and selects the other screen page.
Indexed by the horizontal scroll selector at $13E0. A zero entry suppresses the update. Otherwise this mask is applied before the XOR adjustment at $1539.
Sixteen XOR adjustments paired with the horizontal scroll masks at $14DD.
Indexed by the vertical scroll selector at $13E1. A zero entry suppresses the update. Otherwise this mask is applied before the XOR adjustment at $1552.
Sixteen XOR adjustments paired with the vertical scroll masks at $14FD.
Uses the current direction and step size to index the horizontal and vertical masks and inversion values. Writes the resulting sprite offsets to $33/$34 and composes the VIC display bytes in $29/$2A.
Writes the prepared scroll settings from $29 and $2A to VIC control registers $D016 and $D011. Also saves the low three bits of $D011's value at $27E0.

Loaded bytes $00, $01 and $60 between the return of the scroll register writer and the eight joystick masks. A controlled run to the return at $1570 hit the shadow store at $27E0 with no data accesses in this gap. Its original use remains open.
Eight active-low joystick masks ordered up, up-right, right, down-right, down, down-left, left and up-left. Each mask has the fire bit set.

Polls controls and advances player recovery. On the matching scroll phase and player alignment, refreshes the movement input and chooses a fine-scroll step. When the phase wraps, swaps screen pages, copies the new viewport origin and updates its edges. Continues through timer, display, collision and projectile setup before the optional stage callback.
Calls the alternate-stage update selected by the descriptor at $FCF5–$FCF7.
Low byte of the alternate-stage update address installed from $FCF6.
High byte of the optional stage callback address, patched from the mission descriptor.
Uses the actor selected in $2F. The type byte indexes $9B87 to select the first sprite setup at $1FB8 or $2100. Then advances the sprite slot and calls $203F for the companion.
Uses the actor selected in $30. The type byte indexes $9B87 to select the first sprite setup at $1FB8 or $2100. Then advances the sprite slot and calls $203F for the companion.
Maps nibble values zero through fifteen to status character codes for the two-digit renderer at $16B7. Two additional ascending glyph codes follow the sixteen-entry map.
Takes the value in A and the panel column in Y. Draws both nibbles using the table at $16A5 in the pair of cells at $5370,Y and sets their colours to one.
Operation selector for the horizontal actor-position update at $16F2. It chooses an eight-unit shift for the active actor slots when the view moves.
Zero leaves the actor Y values unchanged, one subtracts eight and two adds eight at $1737.

Uses the current scroll direction to apply eight units of horizontal displacement to the split positions and eight units of vertical displacement to the occupied slots. Clears a slot and calls $9CF1 when its shifted Y wraps.
Initial horizontal character coordinate low byte used to start and restore the full-screen draw.
Initial horizontal character coordinate high byte used to start and restore the full-screen draw.
Initial vertical character coordinate low byte, copied from the mission table at $FCE5 by stage setup.
Initial vertical character coordinate high byte, copied with $1781 into the viewport origin and tile cursor.
Destination screen column for the full-screen draw, passed to the screen and colour store as Y.
Destination screen row for the full-screen draw, selecting the screen and colour row addresses at $1859.

Draws 40 columns by 21 rows starting at the character coordinates from $177F-$1782. Resolves each cell's metatile, then reads the tile colour and the character at the within-tile row and column. Writes both screens and colour RAM through $1856 and restores the initial coordinates.
Immediate offset patched at $17D9. This offset selects the character row in the current metatile.
Writes the selected character and advances the coordinates for the 40-column by 21-row draw. Restores the viewport and lookup coordinates once the last row is complete.

Writes the incoming character from A to the same row and column of both screen pages. It obtains the row addresses from the tables at $9450 and writes the selected tile colour from $05 to the matching colour RAM cell.
Immediate operand of the preceding LDA. The renderer writes the chosen screen code to both playfield pages, then stores the colour in $05 to the matching colour cell.
Zeros the VIC sprite coordinate registers and X high bits. Enables multicolour interpretation for all eight sprite slots, sets the shared colours and clears several four-slot engine state arrays.
Eight masks select one active-low CIA1 port A output per scan, in the order $FE,$FC,$FB,$F7,$EF,$DF,$BF,$7F. The second sample selects two columns.
Eight CIA1 port B samples written in scan order by the keyboard routine at $18D7. A low bit reports a closed switch in a selected column.
Keyboard matrix sample slots for CIA row indices two through four, written by the indexed store at $18F4.
Sixth entry of the keyboard matrix copy at $18CE, read by the key-release wait.
Final keyboard matrix row sample, stored with X=7 by $18F4 and read directly at $140E.
Zero byte following the eight CIA keyboard row samples. The scanner starts at $18D7.
Sets CIA1 A to output and B to input, then applies the eight masks from $18C6 and saves the port B samples at $18CE. The saved X and Y are restored from immediate operands patched on entry.
The keyboard scan restores X from this patched LDX immediate before returning.
The keyboard scan restores Y from this patched LDY immediate before returning.
Active stage display parameter copied from the table at $FCF8.
Alternate-stage flag set at $1A99 and checked at $163C before the patched stage callback.
Flag initialized from the alternate-stage match at $1A9E. The stage-finish path at $1C3A uses it to decide whether to skip its message.
Masks interrupts, maps RAM over BASIC and the KERNAL, initializes the active mission to 1 and calls the mission disk loader before configuring the display.
Turns off the display, selects VIC bank $4000 through CIA2 and caches the bank select with two values for the serial clock line. Stops the CIA2 timers before initial screen construction.
Starts a new player setup, clears score state and saves the current mission for both players. Sets the starting counters using the selected one-player or two-player mode.
Checks whether the active player has lives and whether their stored mission matches the loaded one, before dispatching to the appropriate setup path.

Reads the active player's stage index, selects the alternate graphics when it matches $FCF5, constructs the stage's lookup tables, applies object placements and patches the call at $1AB3 to the mission setup hook.
Copies the low and high target bytes from the current mission's metadata at $FCFE and $FCFF into the operand of the stage setup call at $1AB3.
Calls the stage setup selected by the descriptor at $FCFE–$FCFF.
Low byte of the selected stage setup address, copied from $FCFE.
High byte of the selected stage setup address, copied from $FCFF.

Sets the timer to $03:$00, prepares the selected stage and clears scroll, player-action and outcome state. Selects parameter $52 for mission 5 stage index zero and $7A elsewhere before restoring the player start state.

Draws the starting tile window and builds the stage's working placement state. For the normal display path, initializes the panel, draws the stage message and timer, and writes the target and counter indicators.
Reveals the playfield font, restores the display for the chosen mode, builds the raster schedule and installs its interrupt handler.

Clears $27, the completion-message guard at $BACE, the display phase at $26 and VIC sprite vertical expansion. Enables multicolour on all eight sprites, calls the post-reveal scroll routine and returns early when $9011 is set.
Refreshes the target panel, updates actors and initializes the sprite controls. When $2C equals two, displays message 3 and waits for it to finish.

When $27 is nonzero, saves the active player's placements, shifts the player's remaining-life mask and displays game over if it becomes zero. Wipes the playfield and cycles to the next player with a nonzero mask.
Jump back into the current stage loop at $1AB6.

Displays the stage-complete message and awards the pending score bonus. When the display parameter allows, polls for fire over a countdown, adding score for each pass. Continues to the stage advance logic.
Self-modified immediate operand at $1C63 holding the active clear-screen countdown.

Resets the stage display controls and checks the active player's stage against the special stage index. On an ordinary advance increments the stage and reloads placement seeds. On the special advance resets stage indices, displays a message and increments the player's mission progression.
Copy of actor Y values for sprite setup within the raster handler.
Copy of the active horizontal low bytes for the sprite renderer.
Copy of the active horizontal high bytes for the sprite renderer.
Copy of the secondary horizontal low bytes, consumed by the paired sprite setup.
Copy of the secondary horizontal high bytes associated with $1CB3.
Projectile X low-byte buffer. The stage loop copies it from $0BF0 and the raster path adds the current scroll correction.
Final three low X shadows copied from $0BF0,X. The raster write for sprite three adds the scroll offset to the first of them.
Projectile X high-byte buffer, copied from $0BCA for the raster path.
The last three high-coordinate shadow bytes copied from $0BCA,X. Raster setup fetches the first of these at $2318.
Projectile Y buffer, copied from $0BDC for the raster path.
The last three position shadow bytes copied from $0BDC,X. Raster setup reads slot one's value at $2329.
Eight bytes compared with the sampled keyboard matrix at $18CE by the check at $1CCF.
Compares the eight keyboard scan bytes starting at $18CE against $1CC7. A complete match writes $1F to $0817 and $0818 and returns with carry clear. Any mismatch returns with carry set.
Copies coordinates, actor type and frame values into four-entry raster-facing arrays, including the companion positions and the projectile slots. The interrupt handlers use these saved fields.
Packed BCD bytes indexed by the player score offset at $1D55. The add helper carries toward lower addresses.
Copy of the actors' primary frame indices from $0C11. The raster sprite setup reads the selected slot.
Copy of the companion frame indices from $0C15.
Copy of the additional frame indices from $0C19 for the sprite renderer.
Copy of the actor type bytes. The visibility sorting code uses them when checking the double-sprite flag.
Start offsets into the packed score bytes at $1D3A. The panel selects one with the player index, then draws the packed digits in address order.
End offsets into the packed score bytes at $1D3A. The decimal addition starts at the selected end and propagates carry toward lower addresses.
Adds the input in A to the active player's score and propagates decimal carry through up to four bytes. Saves X and Y before the addition and restores them on return.
Immediate operand for the BCD amount, written by $1D5E. The arithmetic loop continues toward smaller array indices as long as decimal carry remains.
X value patched at the start of the BCD addition. The corresponding LDX restores it before returning.
Y value patched at the start of the BCD addition. The corresponding LDY restores it before returning.
Each pass uses this mask to keep selected pixels in one row of every character in the playfield font. A reverse pass uses its inverse to clear those pixels.
Selects the pixel row (0 to 7) to update on each masked pass through the 256 characters.
Font wipe mode argument. A nonzero value bypasses the mask selection at $1E08.

Runs 32 masked passes across all 256 characters at $4000, each pass touching one row in each glyph. A=0 masks existing destination pixels away. A nonzero takes pixels from $D000, $D800 or $CB00 RAM, selected by $1902 and $ADF7.
High byte of the address in the preceding indexed load. The next path jumps directly to the destination store at $1E1C.

Advances the source and destination by eight bytes, carrying into both high bytes. After the inner count expires, advances the mask phase. When the phase reaches $20, restores processor port $25 and returns.
Places the RAM handler $1E87 in the hardware IRQ vector, sets the first VIC raster compare to $F8, clears pending sources and enables VIC raster IRQs.
Actor slot index selected at $1647. The drawing dispatcher advances it to the adjacent slot for the second draw.

Saves A, acknowledges CIA1 and VIC status, and processes the VIC source bits selected by $28. For a selected source it saves X/Y, reads the raster schedule and replaces the destination of the jump at $1EB6 using the two handler tables.
Low byte of the raster handler target selected by the current raster index.
High byte of the raster handler target selected by the current raster index.
Advances the raster schedule index. A scheduled line of $FF restarts the schedule at line $21CE. Writes the compare register and restores the saved registers before RTI.
Current raster handler index, read at $1E9B to dispatch through the split table and advanced at $1EB9.
Low bytes of handler addresses. The dispatcher indexes with the handler number from the raster schedule and patches the low JMP operand at $1EB7.
High bytes of handler addresses copied into the JMP operand at $1EB8.
Loaded zero byte after the raster handler addresses. The actor sprite IRQ handler at $1F06 clears it before returning to the scheduler.
Raster handler selected by index eight. Writes $17 and $10 to VIC control registers one and two, saves seven in the scroll shadow at $27E0 and transfers control to the common raster scheduler.
Calls the two sprite-programming helpers for the selected actor slot with a short busy wait between them. Clears $1EE6 and continues to the interrupt's common raster scheduler.
Loads the selected slot from $1E86. Applies the screen offsets to the stored position, then writes sprite 5 coordinates, X high bit, colour, both screen pointers and masked priority.
Programs sprite 4 using the selected actor's companion coordinate pair. Sets sprite colour 7, writes the frame pointer to both screens and masks the priority register using $1901.
Slot-specific byte set to two in the launch initializer at $9C55.

Uses the selected slot at $1E86 to program sprites four and five from the buffered coordinate arrays starting at $1CA7. Subtracts the latter sprite's slot height offset, sets pointers and colours, and masks both sprite priorities.

Uses the actor frame to choose horizontal side-by-side or vertically stacked sprite positions. Applies viewport offsets and writes X high bits, two sprite colours and pointers on both screen pages. Applies the actor priority flag and scene mask.
Draws the selected actor's two components with the same stacked or side-by-side layout as $203F, using VIC sprite slots 4 and 5 and their corresponding colour and screen pointer locations.
Updates the selected actor slots through $1675 unless $26 is set. Then counts sprites near the panel boundary through $92C9 and continues to the raster scheduler.
Low eight bits of the first raster compare after the dispatcher restarts the schedule.
Indexed low raster compare values for the dispatcher's return. $FF resets the schedule index and uses the value at $21CE instead.
Handler-table indices parallel to the raster line schedule. Each selected index is copied to $1E86 before dispatch.

Clears the high-numbered sprite Y registers and schedules the alternate action sprite or the actor pair below the split. Schedules the split itself and the second actor row where visible, appends the sentinel and loads the VIC raster compare.
Appends the incoming Y position and actor index to the paired tables at $21CE and $21D5. For Y $DC or higher, except $FF, it substitutes position $FF and index seven after a short delay.

Chooses step four or five from $0AD3. Advances each active projectile in its saved horizontal direction unless its gate or hit countdown is set. A terrain hit or crossing a horizontal boundary starts a three-update retirement timer, which eventually clears the projectile's Y.

Programs VIC sprites 2 and 3 from the projectile positions. Writes high X bits through operands at $233B and $2341, applies priority and rotates normal animation frames. Independently overrides the frame and colour while a projectile's hit timer is active.
Immediate Y operand in the player sprite X-high setup. Its zero test controls whether the next bit is added.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $2340, generated from the high byte and carry of the second projectile's X calculation.
Phase counter for projectile sprite animation. The renderer at $23C8 wraps it at two or three depending on $0AD3.
Clear permits a new shot. The fire handler clears it on release and writes eight on a new shot. The close-range hit handler may set it to twelve.

Tests active-low fire, its hold latch and the movement gate. Uses a free projectile slot and offsets the launch position by 16 or 24 horizontally and by six or 22 vertically. Saves facing and collision flags, starts the effect, and marks the fire latch.

Converts the slot's position to character and then metatile coordinates, retaining the screen-relative character location in the slot arrays. Reads the attribute map and tests its low two bits against the shot's plane mask. On collision starts effect six and returns one, otherwise returns zero.
Three starting columns for the player number field in the auxiliary panel, selected by $257A. The player number and separator precede the score.
Player index selected for score-panel drawing and placement data lookup.
Player-mode value checked against three at setup. The setup subtracts one to initialize the participant countdown at $081A.

Selects the current player panel and writes its number and score. Passes the high and low nibbles of the four stored score bytes to $2601, then sets the two panels' common colour and blinks the active player row using bit five of $25FF.
Panel animation counter. The updater increments it and tests bit five at $25E8.
Score-panel digit-loop flag tested at $25C5 and cleared by the panel setup.
Takes the incoming digit in A and destination offset in Y. Suppresses a leading zero until the flag at $2600 is set. Always advances Y and sets the flag when a digit is emitted through $FB.
Packed decimal seconds. The countdown reloads $59 and borrows from the minute byte when seconds pass below zero.
Packed decimal minutes for the play timer, initialized to 3 by stage entry.
Countdown initialized to $32. Each call of the clock decrements it and the seconds update reloads it at zero.

Counts down from 50 calls, then subtracts one BCD second using decimal mode. Borrows a minute on seconds underflow, and when there are no minutes to borrow sets the timeout outcome and clamps the display to zero.
Stage-message latch. Stage startup sets it before showing text $0B, and stage finish tests it after the message wait.

When $265F is nonzero, draws character codes $10 through $13 in a two-by-two group at $5390 and sets colour five. When zero, preserves the character cells and writes colour zero to the same four cells.
Places the minutes, colon and two BCD second digits in the panel starting at $53BB. Each digit uses the second numeral set at glyph $14 plus the digit.

When the mission stage parameter at $0AEA is zero, resets the count at $0BE0 and both glyph codes to $1E. Otherwise derives the first glyph code by subtracting $16 from the count and the second by adding $21 to that result.
Lower edge of the band the object checks compare against, derived from $0BE0 by subtracting $16 on the path at $26F0.
Other edge of the band, calculated from $26FC plus $21 on the path at $26F6.

Where $0AEA enables the split, clamps eligible nonempty actor Y slots near the divider. Uses $0BE0 plus 12 for the lower group and $0BE0 minus 44 for the upper group. Leaves types with a nonzero flag at $9B87 alone.
NMI setup latch tested before programming CIA2 timers at $277E.
Blanks the display and waits on the raster. On first entry installs $284F as the NMI vector, programs both CIA2 timer latches with $4CC7 and starts timer A at the selected raster position.
Writes zero to both CIA2 timer controls and the interrupt control register, then clears the setup flag at $2771.
Panel IRQ synchronization byte written by the interrupt and compared with one at $280B.
Table that the panel IRQ indexes at $2871 to select the next display operation.
Low three bits of the vertical scroll register saved by $156D for the panel IRQ.
Display flag tested by the panel IRQ before programming the player sprite pointers.

Clears the high display-mode bits and horizontal control, programs the CIA2 timer B latch to $1B58 and starts the timer. Writes two to the display-band state before restoring the port and returning from the interrupt.

Checks which timer B phase is pending. On the playfield path chooses the screen from $2E, restores the background and multicolour display state, and invokes the raster helper when the update gate is clear.
Immediate operand of the interrupted code's saved X. The epilogue reloads both registers before restoring the processor port.
Immediate operand of the interrupted code's saved Y. The epilogue then restores the previous port and A and executes RTI.
IRQ tick byte incremented at $2894 and read by the keyboard-and-joystick routine at $3BCF.

Saves A and the processor port, banks in I/O and tests CIA 2 status bit one. Branches to $2808 for that source. Otherwise saves X and Y in the operands at $28E5 and $28E3 and falls through to the panel interrupt code.
Patched delay operand in the NMI handler at $2864. The handler counts X down before switching the VIC display.
Waits through two delays, switches the character display, signals the game tick and arms CIA2 timer B. Can write the first two sprite frame pointers before restoring the bank and registers.
Immediate operand of the first pointer load. The handler writes the pointer to both screen pages before loading the second pointer.
Immediate operand of the preceding LDA. The interrupt tail writes the second sprite pointer to both screens, sets $27D7, restores Y, X and the prior processor port, then returns from IRQ.
Saved Y in the panel IRQ's final LDY.
Immediate operand of the LDX that restores the interrupted code's X. The interrupt then restores the bank and A before RTI.
Twelve low X bytes seeded from the player at $293F.
Twelve high X bytes seeded from the player at $293F.
Twelve Y bytes seeded from the player at $293F.
Twelve live values initialized from $2927 at $2956.
Twelve live values initialized from $2933 at $295C.
Twelve initial values copied to $290F by $293F.
Twelve initial values copied to $291B by $293F.
Fills the X-low, X-high and Y arrays at $28EB/$28F7/$2903 from the player's position. Copies the two adjacent twelve-byte templates at $2927/$2933 into the live arrays at $290F/$291B.
Bit masks equal to one shifted by the indexed sprite number. Callers use the selected bit when enabling a sprite or setting its X high flag.

Draws a consecutive group of motion records from index $0C8B through the index just below $2A33. Writes the sprite positions, then adds or subtracts the speed magnitudes and changes their direction bits at the horizontal and vertical bounds.
End index of the loop whose indexed store at $2A24 writes $290F,X. The loop exits when X matches this field.
Timer loaded with $28 at $2A52 and decremented at $2AF2.

Requires its request flag and an active-low input bit. Saves the display state, enables all eight multicolour sprites, starts effect nine on two voices and calls the radial animation setup before entering the two-pass sprite display.
Patched immediate operand loaded at $2A89 and written to the VIC sprite multicolour register at $2A8B.

Configures the sprite display and waits for raster ticks. The first pass displays group zero through seven with matched frame pointers. The second selects group eight through eleven and calls the normal raster and player-coordinate helpers before advancing that group.
Dispatches the sprite setup callback patched from the stage descriptor.
Low byte of the sprite setup callback address used at $2B09.
High operand of the optional patchable call at $2B09. The stage descriptor provides this byte at $FCFD.
Patched background colour value written to the shadow at $2D.
Patched value written to the display-phase flag at $26.
Patched interrupt mask immediate written to $28 before returning.
Low bytes of the first sprite frame source addresses, indexed by frame at $2BB4.
High bytes paired with $2B19. The first bulk copy patches its source at $2BC5.
Low bytes of the second sprite frame source addresses. The selector at $2BD5 adds any source offset in $C8.
High bytes paired with $2B4B. The selector at $2BDD adds the high offset and carry.
Starting destination offset for the player sprite preparation loop. The copy at $2BC0 loads it into X.
Selected player pose used to index the sprite layout at $2DF0 and the split source table at $2B19 and $2B32.
Active pose-override countdown. $2B87 selects the override only when this field is nonzero and decrements it on use.
Override pose copied to the normal pose field while the override countdown is active.
Pose saved by sprite preparation for the IRQ and draw path.
First player sprite pointer published for the raster handler. The flipped sprite publishing path sets it to $53.
Second player sprite pointer published for the raster handler. The flipped sprite publishing path sets it to $52.

Uses the timed override at $2B80 and $2B81 while it is active. Saves the chosen frame in $2B82, patches the frame parameter at $2C28 and patches the source load at $2BC5 from the split table at $2B19/$2B32.
Loads one byte from the first player sprite source. Y advances from zero through 62.
Low byte of the first player sprite source address, patched at $2BB7.
High byte of the source address patched by $2BBD. The copy at $2BC5 writes 63 source bytes starting at $5400 plus the offset in $2B7D.
Loads one byte from the second player sprite source. Y advances from zero through 62.
Low byte of the second player sprite source address, patched at $2BDA after adding the base pointer.

High byte of the second sprite source, patched at $2BE2. The loop writes 63 bytes to $5440 plus the sprite offset. On Mission 2 with stage index two, the crop path subtracts player Y from the baseline at $0BD4 and tests the result against sixteen before blanking rows.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $2C27. Controls whether the loop also stores the row into the second buffer.
Toggles the active sprite-buffer half. When facing requires it, mirrors the two newly copied frames through $2C8E. Publishes frame pointer pairs $51/$50 or $53/$52 according to the active half.
Four bytes holding the two high bits in each possible combination, $00,$40,$80,$C0. They immediately precede the two scratch bytes used by the pixel-pair reversal generator.
Input byte shifted right two bits per pass when generating the multicolour pixel reversal table at $4C00.
Output accumulator shifted left two bits per pass at $4C0A. At $4C28 the completed byte is stored in the reversal table.
Mirrors 21 rows of three bytes in the sprite work area at $5400 plus Y. Swaps the outer bytes of each row and reverses their two-bit pixel pairs through the table at $0600.
Six trajectory indices for the sprite effect. Each index selects X and Y offsets from $9492 and $94D2.
Number of trajectory indices to advance in the effect's increment loop at $2D7C.
X-high masks for the six effect sprites, in VIC sprite order from sprite two through seven.
Animation counter incremented at $2D12. The updater shifts it right before saving the result in the operand at $2D21.
Chooses the player pose, derives the effect origin from the current player position, and clears six trajectory indexes. Sets the six sprite colours to one and starts with one active trajectory.

Advances the six sprite positions from the explosion's origin using the offsets at $9492 and $94D2. Cycles sprite pointers, advances each active offset index and adds another trail index at every fourth step up to six. Serves sound while waiting for the animation index to reach $40.
Immediate operand of the instruction beginning at $2D20. Its value feeds the sprite frame selection before the position update.
Temporary sprite mask assembled by the draw routine at $2DA8 and subsequently read into X at $2DE3.

Starts with selector zero, then uses the high byte and low byte of player X to choose bits for the panel mask. Adds a Y-dependent bit, looks up the resulting selector at $2EEB and writes the same mask to $13E0 and $13E1.

Immediate comparison threshold for player Y. Below it, the routine combines selector bit 2 with the flags at $2DA7. Above it, it combines bit 0. At equality, it preserves the existing flags. The result indexes $2EEB for both bytes at $13E0.
Table indexed by the selected frame at $2B9E to patch the parameter at $2C28.
Projectile colours selected by the player index in $39. The path at $2391 reads the indexed colour and writes the corresponding VIC colour register.

Chooses an alternate frame index for recoil or the override at $3B60. The table at $2DF0 selects whether sprites 0 and 1 sit side by side, 24 pixels apart, or share X with a 21-pixel vertical offset. Applies screen offsets, updates the coordinate high bits, sets the colours and masks sprite priority.
Direction masks indexed by the combined facing and position selector at $2DE6. The routine applies the selected mask to both scroll selectors.
Integer component of the player's vertical velocity. The motion step adds it to the player Y together with the carry from the fractional addition.
Fractional component of vertical velocity, added into the accumulator at $2EFA.
Fractional vertical-position accumulator. Its carry from $3A7B feeds the integer Y addition.
Player facing state. The projectile setup copies it into the direction array at $0ACC.

Reads the two horizontal bits in $35. With both set, selects the stationary pose. Otherwise adds or subtracts the step in $38 from the split X position within its screen limits, updates half-resolution X at $0BF6, and picks the movement frame from the pose and animation state.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image up one row. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 0.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image up one row and right one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 1.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image right one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 2.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image down one row and right one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 3.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image down one row. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 4.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image down one row and left one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 5.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image left one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 6.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4800 to $4C00, shifting the image up one row and left one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 7.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image up one row. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 0.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image up one row and right one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 1.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image right one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 2.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image down one row and right one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 3.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image down one row. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 4.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image down one row and left one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 5.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image left one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 6.

Copies 21 rows of 40 characters from screen $4C00 to $4800, shifting the image up one row and left one column. Source indices use one linear screen offset, so the edge cells need redrawing after the copy. The dispatcher at $1465 installs this address for direction index 7.

Converts the player's position to character coordinates relative to the viewport, samples the stage grid at several neighbouring points and stores the collision flags at $39B5–$39B8. Below screen Y $BE it clears the sample flags and returns.
Rise counter used by the vertical-motion integrator. The upper terrain probe at $3997 can seed it from $3992, and the terrain lookup uses it as a vertical offset.
Subtracts the sprite-origin offsets and scales to character units. Adds the viewport origin, then shifts each coordinate two more places into a metatile index.
Zero byte between the position conversion return and the attribute-sample workspace at $394F.
Ten attribute bit-two samples set by $395D, in ascending row order.
Calls $38F7 for the sample position, then starts five rows above it. Reads bit 2 from ten attribute cells in the same column into $394F, substituting zero when the row lies outside the grid.
Five result bytes indexed by the first upper terrain sample that has bit two set.
Rebuilds the vertical terrain samples and tests the first five entries. When a sampled cell has bit two set, copies the corresponding byte from $3992 to $38F6.
Second cached terrain sample, stored at $38B1 and masked to three bits by the scroll check.
First cached terrain sample. The scroll check masks it to three bits at $13F2.
Cached side terrain sample written at $38DF. The obstruction check tests it at $3B3A.
Cached opposite-side terrain sample written at $38F2. The obstruction check tests it at $3B4C.

Converts the two 16-bit character coordinates at $06 and $08 to metatile column and row by shifting right twice. Uses $0896/$08B6 to find the attribute row, then returns the selected column byte in A.
Zero byte between the attribute lookup return and the current player plane at $39E3.
Player plane byte. Projectile setup saves a copy in the shot's plane field.

Uses the rise counter at $38F6 to move the player up first. Otherwise adds the fixed-point falling speed, increases it up to six, and tests terrain for a landing. Stops falling at the aligned ground position or sets the outcome flags when the player reaches Y $DC.
Vertical fine-scroll correction shifted left twice before the player alignment calculation at $3ADC.
Terrain sampling flag set around the call at $3A36. The sampler returns early after saving the second sample when this flag is set.
Motion latch checked at $3B03 before the branch that sets it to one.

When the two movement gates are clear, detects a new active-low up press. If the fire bit is released, writes $F7 and zero to $2EF8/$2EF9 and sets the jump state at $36. Releasing up clears the latch at $3AF2.

Sets both lateral obstruction bits when player Y is $C0 or above. Otherwise reads terrain through $3837 and applies the direction mask at $39E3 to the two samples at $39B7/$39B8 before setting bits 3 and 2 in $35.
Zero byte separating the obstruction-test return from the override field at $3B60.
Special movement and sprite-pose override. The control path at $1597 tests it before selecting the next movement input.
Seven keyboard matrix row indices used by the control merge at $3B8F.
Seven keyboard matrix tests paired with the row indices at $3B61.
Seven active-low clear masks corresponding to the keyboard controls. Each selected mask clears its matching bit in the combined input.
Scans the keyboard, reads joystick port 2 through CIA1 port A and applies seven keyboard masks to the saved control byte. A pressed control clears its corresponding bit in $0ADB.
Immediate X operand at $3BA8. The following path checks the mode flag and keyboard scan bit before displaying selector three and waiting for release.

Rescans the keyboard after the raster line wait. While the colour key is active and the raster tick passes the mask test, increments the active player's colour and updates the first two sprite colours.
Keeps the latest raw masked input in $0ADC. Suppresses player input during the lockout at $0C4D, or sends the input to the demonstration or capture path depending on $9011.
In mode 2 stores a duration and new control byte when the byte changes, then advances the write index and resets the duration.
X restore immediate saved at entry to the merged control reader.
Y restore immediate saved at entry to the merged control reader.
In mode 1 loads an input byte and its duration whenever the previous duration expires. Decrements the duration and applies the saved byte at $0ADB. A zero byte sets $2C to 1 instead.
Immediate operand used to restore X while fetching the next pair of demonstration control and duration values.

Thirty-three active-low control values for the attract demonstration. The playback routine selects them in order and a zero entry ends playback. Mode two replaces entries when the control mask changes.
Thirty-three durations paired with the demo control masks at $3C6E. Playback counts down the selected duration before fetching another entry.
Duration of the current input run in recording mode. Playback loads a saved duration into the same counter and decrements it.
Input run index. The recorder advances it after storing a run, and playback advances it after fetching one.
Previous input mask during recording and active recorded mask during playback.
Samples the keyboard until bit one stays set for eight reads, then waits for the frame flag at $2B and clears it.

Thirty-two initial bytes reached by extending the demonstration duration indexing to runs $3F through $5E. Both duration loads at $3C4C and duration stores at $3C25 can address this span because the index is not masked. The built-in demonstration terminates on the zero control entry at index $20.

Decrements the divider at $0825 and reloads it to five on expiry. Toggles bit 1 at $0820, selects an entry from $081C using the low two bits of $0822 and advances the four-step and six-step counters at $0823 and $0824.

Reads terrain masks, applies acceleration of $0080 until the whole speed reaches eight, and adds the resulting velocity to the actor's fractional and whole Y. Clears Y and actor type on a downward wrap. On landing zeroes velocity, aligns Y to the tile boundary and can reverse direction when the actor returns to its saved X.
Converts the position at $6A through $6C from character to metatile coordinates. Reads the corresponding attribute row and returns bits zero through two of the selected cell.
Six world columns for the colour strips. The renderer subtracts the view's origin column and rejects positions outside the current width.
Low bytes of each last-drawn colour destination, recorded after the stores at $B801 and $B804.
High bytes paired with $3E11. The erase path uses the saved pair before drawing at a new position.
Eight colour values indexed by the integer phase in $3E27. The renderer adds colour bit three.
Per-cell integer phase, incremented by carry from the fractional addition and reduced modulo eight before indexing $3E1F.
Per-cell fractional phase, incremented by the corresponding byte from $3E37.
Increments for the fractional palette phase at $3E2F.
Twelve-byte DOS stream name for drive 8. The digit at $3E45 is replaced from the mission index before opening the file, and the suffix requests a PRG stream for reading.
ASCII mission digit patched into the DOS filename before SETNAM. The next four bytes are comma, P, comma and R.
Resets the KERNAL vectors and initializes I/O, sets the twelve-byte filename at $3E3E, opens logical file 1 on drive 8 with secondary address 3 and selects it for input.

Blanks the screen and disables the current raster and CIA interrupt sources, sets the ASCII digit in the mission filename and opens the disk stream. Reads $0500 bytes to $6400 and $3EF0 bytes to $C000, then closes the stream and restores the saved processor port.
Banks in the KERNAL to close the channel after both transfers. The immediate operand at $3F2B holds the processor port saved before the load.
Processor-port immediate saved by $3EC6 and restored by the loader. The rest of the tail clears both VIC border colours and enables display bit four.
Low byte of the mission receive counter. The loop increments it at $3F68.

Reads one byte through KERNAL CHRIN, banks out I/O and ROM for the store through $FA/$FB, increments that destination and decrements the remaining length in $FC/$FD. Returns when the counter reaches zero.
Four PETSCII bytes spelling @0:I between the receive return and the channel-close entry. The active channel opener instead passes the 12-byte filename at $3E3E to SETNAM.
Closes logical file 1, clears the channel selections and waits for 255 passages of raster line $F8 before returning. Restores X from the patched operand at $3FA4.
Waits for raster line $00F8 and for the low raster byte to change, then repeats that pair of waits 255 times.
Saved X reloaded by the mission receiver's epilogue before RTS.
Zero-filled bytes in the resident program between the disk loader's workspace and the generated tileset window at $4000.
Enumerates all 256 byte values, reverses the order of their four 2-bit fields and stores the result at $0600,X. The table permits horizontal reversal of multicolour pixels.
Operand of the LDX at $4C00. For every input byte, the loop at $4C02 reverses its four two-bit pairs and stores the result in the lookup page at $0600.
High address operand of the load at $4C25, which reads the byte assembled by reversing all four pixel pairs.
Stores the reversed-pair result at $0600 plus the original byte in X.
Low byte of the indexed store destination for the generated reversal page. The loop advances X and repeats until the byte index wraps.
Clears the full page at $0400, then sets its byte at $04A0 to $FF.
Ten 8-byte glyphs for digits 0 to 9 in the custom font, each byte holding the eight pixels of one row.
Eight-byte glyph slots for codes $0A-$1E. The block includes the two-dot separator at $0F and the second set of digit shapes at $14-$1D used by the stage timer panel.
The eight bitmap rows immediately before the alphabet area starts at $5100.
Custom fixed-width glyphs from blank at index $20 through Z at index $3A, eight bytes per character.
Eight zero pixel rows per glyph from index $3B through $5E, following the resident font's capital letters.
Forty loaded space-code bytes between the main font allocation and the auxiliary panel screen.
The first 40-cell row of the auxiliary screen initialized to spaces by $9012. The panel's rows lie at $5320 through $53E7.
Indexed score-panel cell where $2599 writes the selected player number.
Second cell of the panel's second row, immediately after its first cell at $5348.
Thirty cells of the second screen row in the auxiliary panel, starting at column ten.
Third screen row of the panel. The text routine at $BA81 and the two-digit renderer at $16B7 write their selected columns here.
Top-left indicator cell. The indicator routine writes character $10 here.
Second of the two indicator cells on the fourth auxiliary screen row, written by $2660 with the paired cells on the next row.
Start of the remaining-actor panel template drawn by $AA24. Its matching colour cells start at $DB99.
Panel position written by the indexed loop at $990C.
Fifteenth zero-based column of the fourth panel row. The panel count renderer at $AADF writes from this address.
Bottom-left indicator cell. The indicator routine writes character $12 here.
Bottom-right indicator cell. The indicator routine writes character $13 here.
First panel cell written by the timer digit renderer at $2688.
Left edge of the panel's fifth row. The store at $2C31 adds the current column in Y.
Adjacent fifth-row cell used as a base by the companion indexed store at $2C2E.
Third cell in the fifth panel row. Near-actor overlay code at $2C2B writes here during sprite drawing. The panel allocation ends at $53E7.
Eight VIC sprite pointers for the panel screen. Its initializer at $9012 sets each to $55.
Sprite pointer $55 selects this slot in the $4000 VIC bank. The first 63 bytes are zero for the blank frame. The last byte is outside the displayed bitmap.

Multicolour sprite rows for small flying objects and effects, including the pointed projectiles and round flash shapes. Each 64-byte slot holds 21 three-byte rows followed by one byte outside the displayed height.

Multicolour figure poses and component shapes. Upper bodies, leg silhouettes and horizontally paired poses are stored in consecutive 64-byte slots. The mission loader can replace the slots at $6400-$68FF.
Sixteen sprite slots including compact action poses, swinging limb shapes around $5E80 and paired left/right upper-body poses near $5FC0-$6100.
Sixteen sprite slots around the walking and turning poses. Upper- and lower-body shapes are stored in separate frames.
Figure components with long vertical leg silhouettes and mirrored upper body shapes. The first part is in the region the mission loader overwrites.
Upper-body sprites facing either way and long single-leg poses, followed by crouched figures and horizontally extended pieces.
Tail of the actor-frame block, including compact crouching poses and the tall shapes at $6E00 and $6E40.
Sprite rows for figures facing and moving in both directions, including poses with the legs extended and crouching figures.
Standing figures and extended limbs, paired by facing direction across the block.
Last three sprite slots before the larger effect block. These hold mirrored figure fragments.
Sprite slots containing wide silhouettes and bright effect frames, including repeated horizontal pieces and circular bursts.
The final seventeen 64-byte shape slots before the source figure frames at $8000. Each image uses three bytes per row for 21 rows. The last byte of a slot is outside the VIC bitmap.
Upper and lower pieces of large sprite-drawn objects. The last quarter includes numbered award panels.
Last byte of the active VIC bank. Startup clears it at $1974.
Stored 64-byte multicolour frames beyond the live VIC bank. They include repeated figure outlines with altered limbs and matched left and right poses.
Left-facing source frames with poses corresponding to the right-facing art from $8000.
Final resident source shapes beyond the active VIC bank. They include a figure with an extended weapon and large head and body parts.

A 32-byte allocation on the same 64-byte alignment as the six preceding source sprite slots. The first ten three-byte rows are blank except for $44 in the first byte of row seven. Code starts halfway through the slot at $89A0.

Initializes the sprite state and coordinates for slot Y. Selects its plane from bit seven of $FD and stores the placement source fields. Writes the low three placement bits back to the grid before jumping through the type-indexed setup address at $9CB5/$9CC4.
Immediate value for Y before the placed actor's indirect initializer dispatch through $C8.
Polls input and waits for the frame flag, with active-low fire bypassing the wait. Calls the BCD timer decrement and redisplays the digits, then calls the score update. Repeats until outcome two.
Starts ten rows below the top of the view, at colour RAM $D990, and advances to the row alignment selected by $1132 before writing colours.

Converts the selected actor's position and the visible viewport origin into character-grid coordinates. Reads two samples below and two to the sides through $3DE9, writing per-slot masks at $0C25, $0C2D and $8B75/$8B79. Uses mask three left of the map and mask zero below its height limit.
Per-slot attribute samples taken one column left of the starting probe at $8B30, on the probe row two cells above it. Actor movement tests this sample against the orientation mask.
Per-slot attribute samples on the same upper probe row as $8B75, four character columns farther right.
Scans four active actors for horizontal positions outside the permitted region. Clears Y for a retired actor and calls the removal helper, except in types one and five with the per-slot flag set.
Current vertical position for object placement. The initializer copies it into the new actor slot's Y field.
Low bytes of the saved terrain attribute pointers by actor slot. The restoration helper reads these bytes before consulting the corresponding high bytes.
High bytes paired with $8BC5. A zero high byte suppresses the restoration at $9CF1.
Previous attribute cell value saved at $8A0C. The restoration path writes it back through the stored row and column.
Column offset of the saved attribute cell. The restoration routine adds it to the row pointer.
Scratch byte saving the low source pointer from zero page $FB at $8C66. A second initial zero byte lies before the template directory at $8BF9.
Low addresses for the template chosen from the upper four attribute bits on the nonzero-column path at $8CC2.
Sixteen high address bytes paired with the nonzero-column template table at $8BF9.
Final four high bytes paired with the nonzero-column template addresses at $8BF9. Each of these four entries holds $01.
Low template addresses indexed by the four-bit spawn ID when the first attribute column is sampled. A zero low byte skips the spawn path.
High bytes of the addresses paired with the table at $8C1D.
First marker Y captured by the object scan. The deferred spawn handler checks it before counting down $9512.
Second marker Y captured by the object scan. The handler at $9535 tests it.

Derives a tile position from the viewport and examines six rows at its two edges. Low attribute bits feed the edge flags. The high nibble after shifting selects the activation data, and the code allocates a slot for the selected object when it is outside the active Y interval.

Nine loaded bytes after the object scan return, in order $00, $00, $00, $03, $10, $20, $40, $04 and $00. The neighbouring recoil load at $8DAD reads the separate byte at $8D6A. The source of this sequence remains open.
Signed recoil step copied into vertical motion. The recovery code increments it twice at a time.

Chooses a recovery sprite and input override according to the outcome and cooldown. Starts short recoil steps with effect 4, then clears the cooldown and flips facing when the recoil counter reaches zero. A pending loss goes through outcome two and becomes three when its final countdown expires.
Stage setup clears this byte at $1AEB.
Plane-dependent attribute mask. Setup chooses one or two before the indexed stage lookups.
Oldest retained input sample, advanced from $8DFA at $8E3A.
Middle retained input sample, advanced from $8DFB at $8E40.
Newest retained input sample. The handler compares it with the live sample before advancing the history.

Builds an allowed-direction mask from the current plane and stage display parameter. Stores three successive distinct control values and tests for $6F around an intervening $6E or $6D. Calls $3997 on the accepted pattern or when bit five is clear, and enables the special-action override if $3997 sets $38F6. The fallback can seed an ordinary upward motion.

Clears bits 3–7 from height minus one rows of attributes, each row using the stage width. Then examines the active player's placement records until a zero value and counts the records whose type nibble is 1, 5, 9, 13 or 14 into $AA14.
Writes a stage placement value to the address supplied by the current record at $0200,Y.
Low destination address byte from the first byte of the placement record.
High byte of the preceding store's patched address. The logic at $8F07 extracts the four-bit type and increments $AA14 for types 1, 5, 9, 13 and 14 until the record stream ends.
Patches the attribute source from the selected stage's grid pointer. The scan at $8F4D emits placement records into the workspace at $0200, starting at offset $80 when $257A is two.
Loads the current attribute cell using the row address patched into the operand and the column in X.
Low byte of the current attribute row address used at $8F4D.
High byte of the patched indexed map load at $8F4D. The scanning loop advances the two-byte base by the grid width at the end of each row.

Scans the stage attribute grid, extracting cells with any of bits three through seven set. Appends the address and value of each cell to the selected player's half of the placement buffer at $0200 and finishes with three zero bytes.
Byte offset used to restore the previous mark before the next mask is written.
Eight one-bit clearing masks, ordered from clearing the highest bit to clearing the lowest.
Byte incremented or decremented after opposite vertical colour-scroll updates at $1713 and $1731.

For mission 2 with stage index 2, restores the previous byte of the live glyph at $4640 plus $8FA5 to $FF. Combines the fine scroll phase in $33 and $0C57 to compute the new byte offset and select one of eight one-bit clearing masks at $8FA6.
One zero byte between the scroll-glyph return and the stage placement copy entry.
Uses the stage index for player $257A to select the split pointer at $FCE9/$FCED. Copies 128 bytes to $0200 for player one or $0280 for player two.
Controls mode. Mode one uses the built-in demonstration inputs and mode two enables the recorder in the merged-input routine.
Fills the 200 bytes at $5320 with space characters and the eight sprite pointer slots at $53F8 with $55.

Polls input and resets the stack before running the attract sequence. Can reload mission one when entered from a later mission. Sets up the auxiliary display and bonus phase state, then services target, cursor, input and effect helpers on ticks from $2B until phase four. Resets demo state and calls the player initializer before looping back.
Bonus update divider. It reloads six before entering the handler at $B544.
Direction change divider. It reloads $1E before selecting a new direction bit from the random byte.
Direction bit for the bonus position update at $9274.
Bonus flash countdown. The draw path selects colour five while decrementing it.
Offsets added to the doubled X coordinate at $B4FE for the composite bonus figure's sprites.
Offsets added to base Y $AA for the composite bonus figure's sprites.
Frame pointers for the composite bonus figure, written to both screen pages at $919D and $91A0.

Waits for a line in the $A0–$A3 band with the high raster bit clear. Enables sprites zero through four, selects one of two five-entry groups according to the countdown at $9112, and uses twice $B4FE plus per-sprite offsets to set X. Writes the Y offsets, both pointer tables and colour nine.
Shows message eight, then waits on the frame flag. Each pass polls controls and runs the attract handler before decrementing the timer. Finally disables sprite expansion and display.
Immediate X operand at $91CF, patched by $91C1 before the attract input calls. The loop restores and decrements the remaining lifetime.

Clears sprite positions and expansion, then waits for raster $F4 or higher. Shows up to four doubled pairs at fixed X positions with Y positions 42 apart. Writes the two screen pointer sets using frame $FC minus the sprite index as the first pointer of each pair.

High byte of the preceding load. The routine writes the current sprite pointer and its successor to both screen pages. It subtracts 42 from the remaining span and advances the source index by four and slot by two while room remains.
Adds eight to $CC. Once its new value reaches $D4, sets the bonus counter at $AEDE to 100.

Moves $B4FE by three to the left or right according to $9111, changing direction near the ends of the interval. Periodically chooses a new direction from the random helper and calls the launch helper when the separate countdown expires.
Counts enabled VIC sprites 4 through 7 with Y in $BF–$D2. Looks up a value for the count at $932F and writes it to $2865.
Samples the enabled sprite Y registers in ascending two-register steps. When bit six of $18D0 is clear, advances the selector at $2865 and wraps ten to one. Returns the selector in A and $22 in Y.
Count of enabled sprites four through seven whose Y lies between $BF and $D2, inclusive.
Lookup for the eligible sprite count in $932E. The first four results are 9, 6, 4 and 2.
Lookup result for count four. The SID effect updater also uses this address for temporary voice selection.
