Updates the player frames and, outside the demo gate, the score, targets, timer and other panel fields when the raster is below $50. In Mission 3 stage zero, clears the upper actor group and disables the split when the target and viewport checks pass. Calls the attract input helper on exit.

Updates shots, special action, actors, timer, spawns, contact and SID effects in order. At several points it checks $2B and discards its return address when the next gameplay tick has arrived, re-entering the main loop directly.
Eight high-bit masks from $80 through $FF. Each successive byte adds one more low bit to the group of set bits.
Sets the VIC screen and background registers, fills the playfield screen with glyph $29 and colour six and creates a separate fill in the character buffer. Clears $944F before returning.
Scratch byte cleared at $944B before the setup routine returns.
Low bytes of the addresses of 22 screen rows, used by the initial renderer and alternate scenes.
High bytes of the addresses of the same primary screen rows.
Low bytes of 22 colour RAM row addresses. The colour high-byte table starts at $0AB6.
Sixty-four X offsets for the effect around the player sprite. The draw loop indexes each active trajectory independently.
Parallel sixty-four Y offsets for the effect. The draw loop adds the matching entry to the effect's origin.
Delay checked and decremented before servicing the first pending marker at $8C3D.

Waits for an active source and the spawn delay, and skips the alternate scene and Mission 2 stage index two. Uses the selected source height minus 32 and the viewport limits to choose a vacant actor slot. Calls $89A0 with type 3 in Mission 1 or type 6 in other missions, then reloads the delay to $96.
Low bytes of the destination addresses for glyphs drawn as sprite pixels. The glyph writer at $9670 patches the store from this table.
High address bytes paired with the destination cells at $95D4. The glyph writer advances the destination by three bytes between rows.

Clears the text sprite buffer starting at $5400. Walks a zero-ended ASCII message after its leading position byte, converts digits and capitals to glyphs from $5000 and writes eight glyph rows three bytes apart in sprite storage. A digit 1 in these templates uses the active player number at $39.
Stores a glyph byte to the patched text sprite destination with X as the byte offset.
Low destination address byte used by the indexed glyph store.
High byte of the sprite buffer store operand at $9682. The glyph destination table patches it for each character. The loop writes eight rows three bytes apart.
Arranges five expanded single-colour sprites with common Y $58. Starts X at the first byte of the text descriptor and adds $30 for each sprite, updating its ninth X bit and both screen pointers.
Index into the message string. The glyph renderer starts at one and advances it at $968D.
Sixteen split pointers selected by message number in A. Low bytes are at $9702 and high bytes at $9712. Both indices 4 and 5 select the mission-retention prompt.
High address bytes paired with the sixteen low bytes at $9702 for the message selector.
Player-number and game-over text. Starts with position byte $74 and ends at the zero before the ready message.
The ready announcement begins with position byte $7C and includes the player-number placeholder.
Tells the player to wait for a new mission. The position byte is $46.
Announces that time ran out. Its template begins at position $74.
Asks the player whether to keep mission 1. Both corresponding pointer-table entries use these same bytes.
Two-line completion message placed by position byte $50.
Two-line objective text placed by position byte $5A.
Title word with position byte $84.
Bonus heading placed by position byte $50.
Two-line practice or demonstration prompt with position byte $46.
Two-line fire prompt with position byte $46 for the sprite renderer.
Perfect result text with position byte $46.
Stage completion text with position byte $64.
Two-line disk loading text with a mission-number slot.
Standalone message selected by index 15 in the sprite message table.
Sixteen VIC colour values selected by bits 2 to 5 of the message delay counter, copied to the first five sprite colours.
Uses A to select a message pointer from $9702/$9712, sets the message state and calls the sprite renderer.

Waits for the $2B flag and clears it on each pass. Cycles the first five sprite colours and allows controls to dismiss the message after the delay counter drops below $5A. Clears sprite enables, expansion and message state on exit.

For the demonstration or the active attract prompt, converts capitals by subtracting $20 and places the fire and player-count text at $5352/$53A3. Active-low right selects mode 3, left selects mode 2 and fire enters the player setup at $19B5.
Saved X reloaded by the direction handler's final LDX before RTS.
Two zero-terminated strings for the attract prompt. Mode 3 starts 16 bytes into this table for the two-player message.
Zero-terminated fire prompt for the character screen at $5352, separate from the positioned sprite-message template.
Primary VIC sprite pointer for each buffered actor pose. The raster routines store the selected pointer into both screen tables.
Primary VIC sprite colour for the same buffered pose index used by the $997F frame table.
Companion VIC colour indexed by the primary actor pose. The raster routine at $1F3E writes it to sprite five's colour register.
Flags indexed by the current pose. A nonzero entry lets the raster routine at $204D draw two additional sprites for the actor.
Type-indexed flags used to choose the first sprite setup and decide how the resident renderer programs adjacent sprites.
Per-actor action flags. The patrol path sets the flag when its action delay is active. The type-three updater first clears it.
When nonzero, the placement selectors accept the selected slot without the usual occupied-slot comparison.
Chooses the actor selected in $2F or $30 from the stage parameter and the comparison of $8BC4 with $0BE0. Returns $FF in Y when the slot is already occupied and the type does not allow it.

Chooses the slot after the actor at $2F or $30 using the stage parameter and the comparison of $8BC4 with $0BE0. Depending on the type's flag at $9B9A, also checks whether both adjacent slots have nonzero Y and returns $FF in Y if occupied.
Type-indexed initial values copied to the slot at $0C35.
Remaining entries in the type-indexed state table at $9BEC. Stage placement copies the selected entry to $0C35 plus the slot.
Type-indexed initial values copied to the slot at $0C39.
Type-indexed initial values copied to the slot at $0C3D.
Type-indexed initial values copied to the slot at $0C52.
Stores X as the actor type in slot Y. Uses the type to copy four initial values from $9BEC, $9BFA, $9C08 and $9C16 into the actor record.
Clears three actor counters addressed by slot in Y at $0C45, $A1D3 and $9DE0.
Starts the actor's vertical byte at $F0 and writes two to $1FB4 for the slot in Y. Plays SID effect eight twice.
Selects phase zero in $0C45 and clears the two per-slot counters at $9DE0 and $A1D3. The separate entry at $9C71 uses phase one.
Sets A to one and enters the shared phase and counter initializer at $9C65.
Clears the counters at $0C41 and $0C45 and initializes the delay at $A231 to 100 for the slot in Y.
An immediate return entry among the actor initializers. It leaves registers and slot fields unchanged.
Clears four per-slot counters at $0C41, $0C45, $A579 and $A575.
A second immediate return, adjacent to the initializer that clears the type-four state counters.
Sets the actor Y in slot Y to $8BC4 plus five and clears the slot phase at $0C45.
Writes five to the slot flags at $0C29 and sprite index $5F to $0C11.
Stores zero to the phase field at $0C45 for the slot in Y.
Fifteen split entries indexed by actor type. Copies the selected low byte from $9CB5 and high byte from $9CC4 into $C8/$C9 during setup at $89F6.
High bytes of the stage placement handler addresses paired with $9CB5.
Fifteen split update pointers indexed by the actor type from $0C07,X. Entry zero holds a null pointer and is skipped at $9D60. Several nonzero types share the handler at $9DE4.
High bytes of the resident actor update handler addresses paired with $9CD3.
Uses X as the actor slot. When the saved pointer high byte at $8BDA is nonzero, restores the saved value from $8BEF into the indexed map entry and clears the pointer high byte.
Checks all four slots for both nonzero Y and nonzero type. Calls $9CF1 for each slot that passes.

Starts at slot zero, skips slots with zero Y or type, and tests the map restoration flag and type. If the slot timer at $0C49 is active, decrements it and calls $9D85. Otherwise indexes the type dispatch at $9D63.
Takes the actor type in Y and the active actor slot in X. Builds the indirect jump address from the low and high tables at $9CD3 and $9CE2, then jumps through $C8/$C9.
Returns immediately when $2B is 1. Otherwise sets Y to four times the slot index plus one, advances X and continues at $9D24 until X reaches four.
Per-slot flag selecting the initial side test after the collision query at $3D2A. The nudge helper writes zero when it adds two to the coordinate and writes one on the other path.
Calls the collision query, tests the side flags against $0C29,X and either adds two to the split horizontal coordinate or leaves its value unchanged. Updates the per-slot side flag at $9D81.
Two temporary horizontal limits built from the actor's stored spawn coordinate with offsets of $14 and $28. The signed direction state switches at the limits.
High byte of the actor's second patrol comparison position, initialized from spawn X with a signed offset.
Low byte of the actor's first patrol comparison position, initialized at $A060 or $A079.
High byte of the same patrol comparison position, initialized with the carry or borrow from the low byte.
Sixteen base sprite frame indices read with the per-slot phase at $0C35,X divided by four. The handler adds the actor's facing offset from $0C39,X.
Extra copy of the final frame value two after the opening animation table. The phase comparison against $40 at $9EE3 gates the table load to indices zero through 15.
Four per-slot state bytes for the secondary sprite. Zero selects the ordinary actor path. One and two select decreasing and increasing horizontal motion.

Advances the nonzero hit animation counter and chooses its sprite frame from the facing offset and counter. At $10 it either frees the slot or changes the actor to type 9 at its stored spawn coordinate. For an unhit actor it clears the displayed secondary sprite flag, computes horizontal distance and selects the update path.

Enables the secondary sprite and selects one of four images using bits 1 and 2 of its counter. Moves the secondary horizontal coordinate four units per update. A zero counter swaps direction and reloads $40. At $20 the actor resets this secondary phase and starts SID effect 3.

Below phase $40, indexes the opening sprite frames by phase divided by four and advances the phase. At frame index eight, types other than 1 and 14 start the secondary object offset by $14 and play effect 7.

Advances the phase toward $80. Without the player-row condition this moves the actor one horizontal unit toward its stored X coordinate until the low-byte gap is below $1E. Uses the facing-specific walking frame or the close-range frame 2. With the row condition it instead prepares the patrol limits.
Transfers control to the shared actor update at $A16A. The following entry at $A028 selects sprite two before entering that same path.
Stores sprite index two for slot X and jumps to $A16A.
Compares the actor's stored spawn with the other tracked horizontal position. Builds two limits by adding or subtracting $14 and $28 and selects the base facing frame offset.

Updates the auxiliary sprite frame from the shared counter at $0821 or uses $55 after the per-slot trigger. Tests the interaction gates, row mask and horizontal proximity before setting the trigger, starting two effect-1 voices and decrementing $AA14.
One flag per actor slot. The trigger selects the auxiliary image and makes the completed hit animation despawn the actor instead of changing its type to 9.

For slot X, shifts the two coordinate bytes at $0BBD,X and $0BE3,X through carry to obtain the comparison coordinate. Compares it to $0BF6, puts the magnitude divided by sixteen in $0C3D,X with fractional bits at $0C39,X, and selects direction 1 or 2 at $0C35,X.
Four countdown bytes for the handler at $A235. During the count the handler alternates the frame value between $2C and $47 according to parity.

Advances the hit counter and selects frame $4B or $4C from facing. A completed hit animation releases the slot. In the ordinary state, checks and decrements the alternating-frame timer and the wait counter before starting or continuing movement.
Computes the horizontal increment, seeds the two motion bytes with $F5 and $C8 and selects the active movement phase. Clears the movement counter and secondary display flags.
Four movement counters incremented after a horizontal step. The updater stops incrementing at $18.

Refreshes collision flags. When the movement flag is clear it starts a wait and chooses the standing frame. Otherwise, if the collision mask for the selected direction allows it, adds or subtracts the fixed-point increment and selects the corresponding moving frame.

First pointers of fifteen paired sprite frames. Read alongside the next fifteen bytes at $A371, the six unique pairs are $9B/$9C, $9D/$55, $9E/$9F, $A0/$55, $A1/$A2 and $A3/$A4. In the resident sprite bank, the nonblank pairs join two parts of a figure. Pointer $55 supplies a blank sprite for the single-part frames.

Selects frame $12 during the hit animation and frees the slot at count eight. In the ordinary state it checks two delays, chooses facing from the actor and player X coordinates, sets a walking frame and queries collision. A nearby actor facing either direction can enter a timed alternate frame once the row-mask and phase checks pass.
Four per-slot delays that hold movement at $1E or above and block the close-range animation while nonzero.
Four per-slot frame values set to $20 when this handler selects the first facing direction.
Four per-slot frame values set to $24 alongside the primary frame value.

Moves the actor two horizontal units in its selected direction while its slot mask is clear. With an obstruction and no active jump, compares the selected column and height before either reversing or seeding a jump. Jump setup stores a timer of ten, two motion bytes and the starting X low byte in the slot arrays.
Post-contact phase flags by actor slot. When the contact animation reaches eight, the updater sets this flag and takes the separate frame-$2C path on subsequent updates.
Per-slot action cycle counters. On count four the updater changes the horizontal increment to $50 and clears the count.
Per-slot frame adjustment timers. When nonzero the updater decrements the timer and advances the base sprite frame by one.

Handles the actor's hit frames and pause counters. It chooses its facing from the player's split X coordinate and launches a secondary sprite after setting a direction and an initial offset of 21. On retirement it clears the primary Y coordinate once the secondary slot is inactive.

Selects a facing-dependent frame and applies the four-update firing animation. With neither active motion nor a secondary sprite, advances the burst count, launches a shot or starts a pause after four turns.
Chooses the secondary sprite's frame and colour and moves it three units along the split X coordinate. When its edge test succeeds it clears the direction and selects the blank frame $55.

Advances a contact frame to the retirement threshold of eight, or runs the ordinary vertical movement helper. Uses timers at $0C3D and $A474 to delay changes. With no active vertical motion and the facing timer expired, chooses direction relative to the player's split X coordinate and enters $A83F.

For a slot outside the active plane and without vertical motion, selects a frame from the current direction. When the slot's timer at $A83B expires, flips the direction and reloads the timer to a pseudorandom value between 32 and 63.
Copy of the two frame values $2D and $30. The patrol path selects the same values from immediate operands at $A809 and $A812.
Four slot counters used by $A7FB to delay the direction flip.

Sets the frame bases for each facing direction, calls $A480 to move the actor, then checks the active plane and vertical-motion flag. Sets the per-slot flag at $9B96 when the timer at $A474 is active.

With the countdown active, raises the actor by four while the count is above eight. At eight selects the reward frame and, when the slot flag permits, enables the alternate projectile state at $0AD3. Clears the actor Y and calls $1D58 with argument five at expiry. The zero-count path starts from the ordinary animated pose.

Requires the actor orientation mask at $0C29 to match $39E3, then compares the actor half-resolution X against $0BF6. Differences zero through three or $FC through $FF start the $14 countdown, play effect one twice and decrement $AA14.
One-pixel correction flag added during the actor's terrain probing. The movement routine clears it at entry and sets it on a successful first probe.

Uses $0C35,X divided by four to choose the main sprite frame from $61. The flagged path advances that counter and removes the actor at $1A or above. The active path cycles a companion through frames starting at $9C, moves it left by four and delays its next launch using $0C41,X. Sets the slot flag at $0C4E when the actor's X high byte is below the player's, or when high bytes match and the low byte is at least $20 behind.
Remaining active marker count. Placement scanning increments it and the actor retirement paths decrement it.

Selects the ordinary target count or the alternate scene counter and writes the corresponding label and marks into the auxiliary screen. Fills the rest of the label with spaces and starts a delay when the ordinary target count first reaches zero.
Character indices copied to the bottom panel by $AA24. The count copied is the remaining actor count plus four.
Colour indices paired with the character template at $AA86, copied to colour RAM starting at $DB99.
Colour values consumed by the panel drawing loop at $AA6D.
Character values consumed by the message drawing loop at $AA60.

Reads the active player's byte at $0817,Y. After masking to five bits and shifting once, three rotations test the original bits one through three in order. Each bit selects a space or character $0D for one panel cell, written in colour three.

A slot with a nonzero contact flag uses frame $59 and increments the flag. At eight, clears the slot's Y position and calls $1D58 with A=1. Otherwise selects a distant idle frame or starts a jump when the wrapped half-resolution horizontal separation passes the proximity test. While in motion selects the frame from facing and height, and adjusts horizontal position by two.

Uses a sprite base offset of $18 in the alternate scene. Processes damage and vanishing frames before checking the terrain for ordinary movement. The attack timer triggers a jump at $10 and the actor moves three units while airborne where the collision mask permits.

Enables the two hit flags, picks a direction using the player's X position while grounded, and follows the saved direction in the air. Obstacle masks may reverse the next facing and seed the jump timer. Otherwise the actor chooses a stride and animation base by separation from the player.
Patched operand of the subtraction at $AD97. Holds the actor's half-resolution X for the speed threshold test.

Uses a shorter movement step at separation $64 or above. Updates the slot's X position and frame, then checks for proximity when the vertical motion flag is clear. Seeds the contact pose using the saved facing.
Alternate display flag. The glyph wipe uses it to select the alternate source font.
Stores the source target slot for a bonus hit effect. The allocation at $B2A8 records X here indexed by effect slot Y.
Active countdown or delay value by sprite slot. Several bonus updates set this array to time animation changes and clear it when a slot expires.
Horizontal position values for bonus targets. The renderer doubles the value and raises the VIC high-X bit on carry.
Target Y positions by slot. A zero Y suppresses the moving-slot path at $B4C1.
Per-target movement counter set by the target setup and decremented at $B26C.
Signed per-target horizontal increment added to the position at $B266.
Effect slot assigned to each target. The hit allocator at $B2A8 stores the destination slot here.

Prepares a six-row tile grid of width ten at $CD00, programs the bonus palette, and draws its initial display. Fills 160 cells in both screen pages with glyph $FF, fills the corresponding colours with zero and writes eight solid rows into glyph $FF at $47F8.
Sets the phase parameter at $B4FE to $54. Clears both eight-byte arrays at $AE00 and $AE10 and resets $B3B2.
Bonus phase index used to select a handler from the split phase tables at $B08E.
Bonus phase counter. Individual phase handlers initialize it and count it up or down.
Bonus transition parameter. Setup writes the decremented mission-derived value and the transition at $B1BF replaces it with the combined result bytes.
Initial number of bonus targets, loaded from the mission-indexed table at $AF7F.
Per-mission value copied to $AEE0 by the bonus setup at $AF7F.
First result byte copied from $0818 and ORed with $AEEA in the phase tests.
Second result byte copied from $0819, tested together with $AEE9.

Waits for raster $F8, blanks the display and prepares the alternate scene. Copies four pages of font data from $5000 to $4400, saves the two player progress bytes at $0818/$0819 and picks a mission parameter from $AEE2. Starts phase eight with $AEDE set to 100, then waits within the $D4–$D7 raster band before dispatching on $AEDD.
Calls the bonus phase handler selected by the phase byte at $AEDD.
Low address byte installed by $AFBC from the selected entry in the table at $B08E.

High byte of the phase-selected JSR target patched at $AFC2. The following code waits while the raster is between $D4 and $E3, advances SID effects, then tests the two remaining counters and phase six before leaving the bonus loop.

Clears $27E1 and $26, advances the mission number and loads the next file. Restores VIC bank settings, clears colour RAM and waits for fire before clearing sprite enables and reinitializing the next scene.
Fills the front screen and auxiliary panel's first 160 bottom-panel cells with $04's character value. Writes colour zero for the same cells.
Rotating bonus target slot index. The allocator advances it when the tested slot is busy and wraps at three.
Bonus spawn counter whose low bit chooses the side of the screen.
Ten split addresses with high bytes at $B098. The raster loop at $AFB6 selects a phase using $AEDD and patches its call operand at $AFC6.
Ten high address bytes for the bonus raster loop phase handlers. The low-byte table starts at $B08E.
Runs the bonus player update at $B4FF, the shot processing at $B591 and the target check at $B4BF.
Increments $AEDE. On wrap it selects phase 2 and clears horizontal and vertical sprite expansion.
If enabled by $B1E6, waits for the active-low fire bit at $0ADB. A press sets up the target count, a delay of 100 and phase 8, and clears the enable flag.

Updates the target sprites and shot processing. When the pending spawn count and the active target count are both zero, it selects phase 9, displays message 12 and starts a 100-tick delay. Otherwise it goes through the ordinary player and target update.
Updates the target and attached sprites, processes shots, then reads the input bit at $18D5. A cleared fire bit returns the phase to 2.
Calls $91E0 and decrements a nonzero delay. When the delay expires, switches to phase 5 and calls $B669. An already zero delay takes the $9263 path.
Increments the delay byte and runs $B680 on odd values with its selector operand set to zero.
Selects phase 7 and calls $B669 when either player has a pending bonus flag. Otherwise selects phase 6, the phase the outer raster loop checks for exit.
Increments the delay byte and runs $B680 on odd values with its selector operand set to one.

At delay 100, clears player one's pending flag if set, or player two's, and prints the message using that player number. At delay expiry, recomputes the combined flag, prints message 7, resets the spawn count and enters phase 1.
Counts the delay down to zero, then selects phase 5 and calls $B669.
Gate tested before phase 2 polls fire. Cleared when phase 8 takes over.
Pending target count. It is decremented on allocation of a free target slot and checked with the active count to detect the end of a round.

With spawns pending, checks one of three slots for a zero state. Initialises a free slot at Y coordinate $48, chooses an edge and horizontal step from the parity of $B08D, and draws its lifetime from the low six random bits plus ten. Advances the candidate slot on a busy slot.

With a nonzero lifetime, selects one of the paired advancing frames and writes both screen sprite pointers. At lifetime zero it selects frame $D5, claims an auxiliary sprite slot if available and advances to state 2.
Immediate sprite pointer base patched by $B27D. Bit 2 of the slot value at $AE08 selects one of the two adjacent frames written to both screen pages.
Sets the source slots' two sprite pointers to $D5, then tries slots three and four for the new effect. A free slot gets a six-count timer, a $55 sprite and a link back to the original slot.

Selects frame $D5 and clears the attached sprite's pointer to $55. Outside phase 3 it subtracts two from the target's Y coordinate, switching to state 3 and zeroing that coordinate when the result is below six.
Displays frames $DE and $DF in the paired slots. Outside phase 3 it adds four to the Y coordinate. At $5A or above it advances to state 4 and chooses the motion step using three random bits.
Eight possible horizontal steps for state 4. The random index selects alternating +1 and -1 in the first six entries and zero in the last two.

Writes adjacent frames to the target and auxiliary sprite pointers on both screens. Outside phase 3 it adds the horizontal step. The position thresholds and lifetime determine when to reverse a zero step to -1, switch to state 5, or release both slots.
Patched base-frame operand in the ADC at $B368. The handler adds the position-dependent frame offset before programming the paired sprite pointers.

Writes a frame and its successor to both screen pointer tables for the paired targets. Tests X against the inner and outer limits to update the timer, request a turnaround, switch state or clear both slots.
Byte explicitly cleared by the bonus slot reset at $AED7.
Selects frames $DE and $DF for the target and attached sprite. Outside phase 3 it subtracts eight from Y. Below nine it resets the slots, selects phase 4 and sets $CC to $28.
Split call addresses for target states 1 through 5 with high bytes at $B3EF. Entry zero is zero and is skipped by $B423.
Six high bytes of target renderer entry points, paired with the low bytes at $B3E9.
One bit per VIC sprite. The bonus sprite loop uses these to enable individual sprites and to set their X coordinate high bits.
Active bonus target count rebuilt by the renderer. The phase updater tests it after the spawn quota reaches zero.

Clears the sprite state and scans the three target slots. For each visible state enables its sprite and patches the frame-selection call from $B3E9/$B3EF. Programs the resulting slot's X, ninth X bit and Y.
Low byte of the target-state JSR address. The renderer writes it at $B43D from the low table at $B3E9.
High byte of the target-state JSR address. The renderer writes it at $B443 from the high table at $B3EF.
The renderer saves the slot in the LDX immediate before the handler call and reloads it for the coordinate writes.

Patched immediate Y operand for the LDY at $B454. The renderer saves Y here before the state-specific call. The following sprite update writes the doubled X byte and its carry to VIC X and X high, then writes Y from $AE10.
For state six in slots three or four, follows the parent slot index at $ADF8. Positions the child sprite 21 pixels below its parent when the sum stays within a byte, with colour $0E.
For each active slot in $AE10, subtracts eight from its Y position until below $48, then starts a countdown of five and plays effect six. When that countdown expires, clears the slot.
Bonus aim position. The update moves it in the selected direction and reverses near its bounds.
Sends automated control to $9274 when the demo flag is set. Otherwise polls the player and moves the half-resolution cursor by three within its left and right limits. Uses a fire latch for launching.
Frame selectors by slot, initialized by $B56E. The renderer uses each selector to index $B581.
Per-frame pointer offsets read through the selector at $B5DA. The draw loop adds $30 before writing the finished sprite pointer to both screen pages.

Iterates sprite slots five through seven and draws each active slot from the stored coordinates. For the ordinary case looks up a frame through $B577/$B581. Otherwise converts the slot state to a frame index and changes the sprite colour to seven.
High byte of the preceding indexed load used to select a sprite frame. The rendering loop adds $30, writes its sprite pointer to both screens and advances to the next slot.

Tests active projectile slots five through seven against target states one and four. Requires wrapped vertical and horizontal differences inside both windows. Starts effect zero, clears the target and clears its paired slot for state four. Sets the projectile slot to state five on a hit.
High byte of the preceding store's operand. The collision loop sets target and linked slot counters, iterating three inner and eight outer slots.
Sets $C8 to 20, clears VIC sprite enables and fills all eight rows of the final playfield glyph at $47F8 with $FF.
Bonus diagonal-render selector set to zero or one before the call to the reveal routine.

Processes symmetric columns on successive rows. Writes glyph $FF and colour two, or restores a character from the alternate screen and sets colour eight according to $B67F. At the end of the sweep advances the bonus scene phase.
Companion VIC sprite pointer indexed by the same buffered pose as $997F. The raster routines publish it to both display pages.

Runs for mission five with stage index one. Restores up to six previous colour positions, then uses the viewport to locate visible pairs and writes a colour selected by each pair's animation accumulator. Uses a viewport-indexed bit mask to set the player sprites' VIC priority.
First 16 bytes of the 32-byte threshold bitfield indexed by the horizontal cell at $B82E. The finer index selects a bit and, when set, raises the priority mask for sprites zero and one.
Last 16 bytes of the bitfield at $B841. The bonus setup writes the first byte of this half at $AF1C.
Highest attack slot to test. The hit scanner initializes it to one and raises it to two for the short-range press test.

Starts from the two projectile slots. When fire is pressed and the attack gate allows it, also uses a third test slot at player Y minus six and X plus or minus 24 depending on facing. Scans four actors for activity, type, facing and X/Y overlap, then applies the matching hit rule.

A hit from slot 2 writes a wound flag, starts a cooldown and can clear one pending projectile. Hits from the other slots set their hit countdown and check the actor's type, relative height and damage flags before marking a wound.
Steps through four actor slots for each tested attack slot. After the last actor it decrements X to test the next attack slot or returns when X becomes negative.
Zero-terminated text drawn to the auxiliary status row. The selector at $BA81 looks up a source offset and a starting column, then converts each non-space byte to the local glyph index.
Maps text selectors to their starting offset in the string data at $BA12.
Maps text selectors to their first column relative to $5370.

Uses A as a text selector below eleven. Selects the string and panel columns from $BA67 and $BA74, maps ASCII letters down by $20 while preserving spaces, and writes the characters with colour seven. Restores X and Y from patched operands.
The panel text printer's saved X, restored in the final LDX.
Patched Y restore value in the text routine's final LDY.
Immediate column limit of 40 for the loop that clears the text row with space codes.
Delay initialized to $50 at $AA4E and decremented by the handler at $BAD9.
Latch set when the delay at $BACD starts, tested before starting it again.
While the mode at $1902 is zero and the message timer is nonzero, decrements the timer and passes selector zero or eleven to $BA81 according to timer bit two.
Horizontal contact threshold on one side of the player, compared against the computed difference at $BB63.
Horizontal contact threshold for the other facing-relative comparison at $BB4E.

Skips contact while $0C4D is nonzero. Scans four actor slots for status, type and overlap using half-resolution X and facing-dependent Y limits. A close contact can set $27 and the player cooldown before calling $BBF1. A separate test uses the companion coordinates, type table $9B87 and height offsets at $1FB4.
Ten consecutive multiples of five from zero to 45, between the contact scan return and the effect handler. Their consumer remains open.

Starts SID effect 4 and sets the player cooldown to $20. Types 2, 10 and 11 also set the loss flag and shorten the cooldown to $17. Type 8 sets the slot's contact flag. Most other types seed hit motion and a timer, and the helper sets the player recoil state if $27 is clear.
Ten sequences of sixteen high frequency bytes. The effect updater uses the effect number times sixteen plus the current step and copies the result into the selected voice's high frequency register.
Ten SID control bytes indexed by effect ID. $BD69 writes the selected value after clearing the chosen voice control register and setting its frequency and envelope.
Ten SID attack and decay settings indexed by the effect ID and written at $BD5E to the selected voice.
Three per-voice cursors. Starting an effect resets the selected cursor to zero and the updater advances it until it reaches sixteen.
The three register-group offsets 0, 7 and 14 used to address the selected SID voice.
Three effect IDs indexed by voice. The update routine multiplies the ID by sixteen to select a sequence in the frequency table at $BC5C.
Round-robin slot selector advanced on each effect start and wrapped at three.
Holds the effect argument from A while the slot selector advances.

Takes the effect ID in A and rotates through the three SID voices. Sets volume to 15, resets the slot cursor, and programs the selected voice's frequency, envelope and control. Preserves X and Y through patched immediate operands.
Saved X restored by the effect starter after it programs the SID voice.
Saved Y restored by the effect starter after it programs the SID voice.
Temporary byte holding the selected effect ID times sixteen, used to add the step index before the load from $BC5C.
Visits all three voices and skips a voice whose step is $10. Otherwise advances the step and replaces the voice's frequency high byte from the sixteen-entry sequence selected by its effect number.
The resident load ends with 603 zero bytes after the SID routines.
